case_text:
Vignette:
A 68-year-old male farmer presents with a slowly growing lesion on his nose that he first noticed approximately 8 months ago. The lesion has gradually enlarged and occasionally bleeds when he washes his face but heals over. He has extensive sun exposure from decades of outdoor work and a history of multiple sunburns in his youth. He has never had skin cancer before. On examination, there is a 1.2 cm pearly, dome-shaped nodule on the left ala of the nose with a rolled border and central depression. Multiple telangiectasias are visible on the surface. The surrounding skin shows significant solar damage with actinic keratoses on the forehead and ears. There is no palpable cervical or preauricular lymphadenopathy. A dermoscopic examination reveals arborizing vessels and blue-gray ovoid nests.
